items.name: Pointer
items.docs:
A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901), split on `/`: `/meta/y/z` is `["meta",
"y", "z"]`, and `""` is the whole row. A part is a key as it is:
SurrealDB 4 writes a `/` in a key as `~1` and a `~` as `~0`
(verified on 4.0.1), and `pointer` reads them back.
items.head: Pointer

items.name: pointer
items.docs: The parts of a pointer. A pointer other than `""` starts with `/`.

items.name: pointer_text
items.docs:
The text of a pointer: each part after a `/`, with `~` written as
`~0` and `/` as `~1`.

items.name: Op
items.signature: [Add(Pointer, Cbor.Value), Remove(Pointer), Replace(Pointer, Cbor.Value), Change(Pointer, TextPatch)]
items.docs:
One op of a patch, in the order of the patch. `Change` edits a
string in place with a text patch.
items.head: Op

items.name: op_of
items.signature: { op : Str, path : Str, value : Try(Cbor.Value, [Missing]) } -> Try(Op, [BadOp(Str)])
items.docs:
An op as the server sends it: `{ op, path, value }`. A `value` of
`NULL` is no key in the map, and is `Cbor.Value.Null` here.

items.name: path_of
items.docs: The pointer of an op.

items.name: apply
items.docs:
The value after the op. A part of a pointer is a key of a map, or an
index of an array; `-` is the end of an array for `Add`. `Add` puts
a value in an array before the index, and in a map sets the key.
`BadPath` is a pointer that the value does not have, and `Mismatch`
a text patch that does not fit the string.

items.name: Edit
items.docs: What an op does at the end of its pointer.
items.head: Edit

items.name: edit
items.signature: Cbor.Value, Pointer, Pointer, Edit -> Try(Cbor.Value, [BadPath(Pointer), Mismatch(U64)])
items.docs: The value with `edit` done at `rest`, the part of `path` that is left.

items.name: vmap
items.docs:
A CBOR map of the pairs, in their order. A later key replaces an
earlier one.

items.name: set_key
items.signature: List((Cbor.Value, Cbor.Value)), Str, Edit -> List((Cbor.Value, Cbor.Value))
items.docs:
The entries of a map with `key` set (`Insert`, `Put`) or removed
(`Drop`). A new key goes at the end.

items.name: at_index
items.signature: List(Cbor.Value), Str, Pointer, Edit -> Try(List(Cbor.Value), [BadPath(Pointer), Mismatch(U64)])
items.docs: The items of an array with the edit at the index `key`.

items.name: replace_at
items.docs: The items with the one at `i` replaced.

items.name: index_of
items.docs: An index below `size`, written in ASCII digits.

items.name: Part
items.docs:
One part of a hunk: text that both versions have, or that only the
new or only the old one has.
items.head: Part

items.name: Hunk
items.signature: { at : U64, before : U64, after : U64, parts : List(Part) }
items.docs:
One hunk of a text patch. `at` is where it starts in the text after
the hunks before it, in Unicode scalar values from 0. `before` and
`after` are the lengths of the old and the new text it covers.
items.head: Hunk

items.name: TextPatch
items.docs: A text patch: the hunks, in order.
items.head: TextPatch

items.name: read_line
items.docs: One line of a patch, added to the hunks read so far.

items.name: header
items.docs: The header `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` of a hunk, with no parts yet.

items.name: range
items.docs:
`a,b` as a start from 0 and a length: `a` alone has length 1, and a
length of 0 has its start from 0 already.

items.name: digits
items.docs: A number of ASCII digits only.

items.name: checked
items.docs: A hunk whose parts have the lengths of its header.

items.name: old_text
items.docs: The scalars a hunk covers in the old text: what it keeps and deletes.

items.name: new_text
items.docs: The scalars a hunk gives in the new text: what it keeps and inserts.

items.name: scalars
items.docs:
The UTF-8 bytes of each Unicode scalar value of a text: a scalar
starts at each byte that is not `10xxxxxx`.

items.name: apply_hunk
items.docs: One hunk applied to the scalars of the text.

items.name: unescape
items.docs: The text of a part: `%XX` is the byte `XX`, and the bytes are UTF-8.

items.name: parse
items.docs:
The hunks of a patch in the diff-match-patch text format: a header
`@@ -a,b +c,d @@` per hunk, then one line per part, which starts
with ` ` (keep), `-` (delete) or `+` (insert). A position counts
Unicode scalar values from 1, and a length of 0 counts from 0. A
length of 1 is left out of the header. The text of a part is UTF-8
with `%XX` escapes (`%0A` is a new line, `%25` is `%`).

items.name: apply
items.docs:
The text with each hunk applied, in order. The text must hold the
kept and the deleted parts of each hunk where the hunk starts:
`Mismatch(at)` gives that position when it does not.

items.name: State
items.docs: What the derived encoder threads through: the values built so far.
items.head: State

items.name: Item
items.docs:
One value on the stack. `Fields` is a record, and only `encode_record`
pushes it: the encoder of a record type, or of a nominal of the app over
a record. So the type of a union payload picks its form (`tagged`), not
the shape of its value.
items.head: Item

items.name: Format
items.docs:
The format the encoder is derived against. `I128` and `U128` have no
method here on purpose: a row that holds one does not type-check where
it is written, because SurrealDB has no 128-bit integer. A sized number
is the value of its type (`U8` is `5u8`), so a table with no schema
stores the type of the Roc field. `I64` is `int`, `F64` is `float`.
items.head: Format

items.name: encode_id
items.docs:
A record id, written by the hand-written encoders of `Surreal.Id`
and `Surreal.Link`.

items.name: encode_ref
items.docs:
A record id with a key of any value, written by the encoder of
`Surreal.Ref`.

items.name: encode_datetime
items.docs: A datetime, written by the encoder of `Surreal.Datetime`.

items.name: encode_geometry
items.docs:
A geometry as its GeoJSON object, written by the encoders of the
geometry types of `Surreal`: a `Geometry`, whose literal is the
object, which SurrealDB reads as a geometry, and whose CBOR is the
geometry tag.

items.name: encode_value
items.docs:
A value of a SurrealDB type that has no Roc type, written by the
encoders of `Surreal.Regex`, `Surreal.Date` and the like.

items.name: encode_record
items.signature: Encode.State, U64, (Encode.State, (Encode.State, Str, (Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])
items.docs:
Each field pushes its name, then its value. A field that is absent
pushes nothing, so the key is left out.

items.name: encode_list
items.signature: Encode.State, U64, (Encode.State, (Encode.State, (Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])

items.name: encode_tag
items.signature: Encode.State, Str, U64, (Encode.State, (Encode.State, (Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])
items.docs:
The union payload rule: no payload is the bare tag
name, a record payload is spread next to `kind`, one other payload
is `value`, several are the array `value`. A record is a payload
that `encode_record` wrote (`Item`).

items.name: Bind
items.docs:
The format a captured value is bound in where its type may hold an
opaque type of another package (`Code.Binds`, `Query.filter_with`).
The compiler runs the value's own `encoder_for` against it while the
program runs and hands the bytes to the translator, which reads them
back as the `Ql.Value` that `Encode.Format` gives for the same calls
(`Encode.bound`). Each value is a kind byte, then its contents: a text
is its byte count (8 bytes, big-endian) and its bytes, an integer 8
bytes, a `Dec` its attos in 16, a float its bits in 8, and a record, a
list and a tag hold their members up to a `0`. A sized integer is a
`10`, the byte of its type (`Encode.sized_kinds`) and 8 bytes, and an
`F32` an `11` and its bits in 4.
items.head: Bind

items.name: encode_record
items.signature: List(U8), U64, (List(U8), (List(U8), Str, (List(U8) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])
items.docs:
Each field is a `7`, its name, then its value. A field that is
absent writes nothing, so the key is left out.

items.name: encode_list
items.signature: List(U8), U64, (List(U8), (List(U8), (List(U8) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])

items.name: encode_tag
items.signature: List(U8), Str, U64, (List(U8), (List(U8), (List(U8) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])

items.name: put_sized
items.docs: A sized integer: `10`, the byte of its type, and its 64 bits.

items.name: sized_value
items.docs: The value of a sized integer of `put_sized`.

items.name: big_endian
items.docs: The low `width` bytes of `bits`, the most significant first.

items.name: bound
items.docs: The value of the bytes `Bind` wrote for one captured value.

items.name: read_item
items.docs: The item that starts at `at`, and where the next one starts.

items.name: read_fields
items.signature: List(U8), U64, List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value }) -> Try((List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value }), U64), [BadBytes])

items.name: read_bits
items.docs: The `width` bytes at `at`, big-endian.

items.name: value_of
items.signature: a -> Try(Ql.Value, Ql.Error) where [a.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (a, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs: Encode a value the way a row is written.

items.name: fold_above
items.docs: The stack above `base` becomes one value on top of what was below.

items.name: pair_up
items.signature: List(Encode.Item), List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value }) -> List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value })
items.docs: Names and values alternate on the stack, as `encode_record` pushed them.

items.name: value
items.docs: The value of an item: a record is an object.

items.name: tagged
items.docs:
One union value from its tag and the payloads the arm carried. Only a
record payload is spread next to `kind`. A geometry is an object too,
but its type is not a record, so it is `value`, as the schema and the
reader have it.

items.name: Row
items.signature: { id : Str, qty : I64, price : Dec, ratio : F64, ok : Bool, tags : List(Str), note ?: Str, pay : [Cash, Card({ last4 : Str }), Check(I64), Wire(Str, I64)] }
items.head: Row

items.name: Auth
items.signature: { who : [Basic({ user : Str, pass : Str }), Bearer(Str), Anonymous], scope : [Scope({ ns : Str, db : Str }), FromToken] }
items.docs:
Who a post is from (`who`), and its namespace and database
(`scope`). `Basic` is a system user. `Bearer` is the token of a
record user (`signup`, `signin`) or of `authenticate`. `Anonymous`
is a post before a signup or a signin, and after `invalidate`. A
token holds its namespace and database, so a session of a token
alone sends none (`FromToken`): SurrealDB 3.3.4 runs a post with a
`Bearer` token and no `surreal-ns` in the token's (verified).
items.head: Auth

items.name: Post
items.signature: { uri : Str, headers : List({ name : Str, value : Str }), body : List(U8) }
items.docs: One post, as the platform sends it.
items.head: Post

items.name: post
items.docs:
The post of one RPC message to `url`, the base of the server, such
as `http://127.0.0.1:8000`: CBOR v2 (`application/cbor; v=2`) both
ways, the authentication of `auth`, and its namespace and database.

items.name: reply
items.signature: { status : U16, body : List(U8) } -> Try(List(U8), [Refused({ status : U16, message : Str })])
items.docs:
The RPC reply in a response. SurrealDB answers a request with status
200, also a request whose method or statement fails: the message
holds that error. Any other status is the server refusing the post,
such as 401 for a password that does not verify, with a text body:
the status, and the text, or `HTTP <status>` when there is none.

items.name: Mode
items.docs: What a plan does with a table or a field that the schema dropped.
items.head: Mode

items.name: Plan
items.signature: { steps : List(Schema.Step), old : List(Str), new : List(Str), from : Str, replaces : List(Str) }
items.docs:
The diff from the snapshot `from` (its statements `old`) to the
statements `new` of a schema. `replaces` names the files that a
squashed file takes the place of.
items.head: Plan

items.name: Item
items.docs: A statement of a section, and what a person must write in it first.
items.head: Item

items.name: Warning
items.signature:
[
		TypeChanged({ table : Str, path : Str, from : Str, to : Str }),
		MaybeRenamed({ table : Str, from : Str, to : Str }),
		UniqueAdded({ table : Str, index : Str }),
		AssertAdded({ table : Str, path : Str }),
		NoDefault({ table : Str, path : Str }),
		Rewritten(List(Str)),
		ViewRebuilt(Str),
		Dropped(Str),
	]
items.docs: What a person reads before a migration file runs.
items.head: Warning

items.name: File
items.signature: { name : Str, replaces : List(Str), sections : List(Str), checksum : Str }
items.docs:
A migration file as the runner reads it: each section is the text
between two `-- reify: commit` lines.
items.head: File

items.name: Row
items.signature: { name : Str, checksum : Str, sections : U64, done : U64 }
items.docs: A record of the history table `_reify_migration`.
items.head: Row

items.name: Action
items.docs:
What the runner does with a file: run its sections from `from`
(counted from 1), or record a squashed file whose replaced files
the database applied (`Adopt`).
items.head: Action

items.name: lines
items.docs: The statements of a snapshot: its `DEFINE` lines.

items.name: hash
items.docs: The SHA-256 of a text, as hex.

items.name: sections
items.docs:
The sections of a plan. Section 1 has every step. Section 2 has
what SurrealDB 4 refuses in a transaction that writes to or
migrates a table: an index on such a table, a view over a table
that a `MIGRATE` converts (removed in section 1), and a `REBUILD
INDEX` for each full-text index of a changed analyzer. A plan with
no statement has no section.

items.name: migrated
items.docs: The tables that a `MIGRATE` converts.

items.name: rebuilt_views
items.docs:
The views over a table that a plan migrates: SurrealDB 4 refuses
`MIGRATE EXISTING ROWS` on such a table (verified).

items.name: view_source
items.docs: The table after the first `FROM` of a view.

items.name: rebuilds
items.docs:
`REBUILD INDEX` for each full-text index whose analyzer changed and
whose own text did not: a changed analyzer does not reach the index
that is there (SurrealDB 4 upgrade guide).

items.name: items
items.signature: Schema.Step, { drop : Bool, seed : Str } -> List(Migrate.Item)
items.docs: The statements of one step.

items.name: migrating
items.signature: Str, Str, Str, Str, Str -> Str
items.docs:
A `DEFINE FIELD` with `MIGRATE EXISTING ROWS`: a name of its own,
since SurrealDB 4 runs each name once.

items.name: referenced
items.docs:
SurrealDB 4 refuses `MIGRATE EXISTING ROWS` on a `REFERENCE` field
(verified): such a field needs steps that a person writes.

items.name: castable
items.docs: A type that a cast `<type>` converts to.

items.name: snapshot
items.docs:
The snapshot after the plan: the statements of the schema. With
`KeepData` the dropped tables and fields stay, so that a later plan
drops them.

items.name: dropped
items.docs: The tables and the fields (`table.path`) that the schema dropped.

items.name: warnings
items.docs: What a person reads before the file runs.

items.name: warning_text
items.docs: A warning as the comment of a file.

items.name: file
items.docs:
The text of a migration file: the header, the warnings as
comments, then the sections, split by `-- reify: commit`. A
statement that needs a value has a `-- reify: edit` line before it.
The header names the target `V4`, SurrealDB 4 at compatibility
level 4: the one target there is, kept in the text for a later one.

items.name: parse
items.docs:
A migration file, read: the header, the sections, the checksum.
A `-- reify: edit` line, a `BEGIN`, `COMMIT` or `CANCEL`, and an
index and a write on one table in one section are refused. The
header must have `target V4`. A file with `target V3` (written by
0.0.3 and before, for SurrealDB 3) is `Legacy`.

items.name: is_name
items.docs: Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`: a key of a record id as it is.

items.name: index_with_writes
items.docs:
A table that the lines of a section define an index on and also
write to or migrate, by the first words of each line.

items.name: decide
items.signature: List(Migrate.Row), List(Migrate.File), U64 -> Try({ actions : List(Migrate.Action), ahead : List(Str) }, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
What the runner does, from the history and the compatibility level
of the database, which must be 4 (else `Level`): each file
that is not applied runs, a partly applied one goes on from its
next section, and a squashed file whose replaced files the
database applied is recorded only. `ahead` names the records of the
history that no file of the list has or replaces: a newer app
applied them.

items.name: record
items.docs: The record of a file in the history.

items.name: request
items.docs:
The request of section `k` (from 1) of a file: one transaction that
first marks the section in the history, then runs it. Section 1
creates the record, so a second runner fails on it; a later
section first checks that the record is at the section before.

items.name: adopt
items.docs: The record of a squashed file whose replaced files the database applied.

items.name: bootstrap
items.docs:
The history table, the level of the server and the history, in one
request. Each `DEFINE` is `IF NOT EXISTS`, so it costs nothing after
the first run. The last two results are the level and the rows. A
history of 0.0.3 or before keeps its `target` type, `'V3' | 'V4'`,
which takes the `'V4'` that the runner writes.

items.name: level_of
items.docs:
The compatibility level that `bootstrap` reads. SurrealDB 3 has no
level: `none`, and the error says that it is not SurrealDB 4.

items.name: Error
items.signature: [Unsupported(Str), BadSchema(Str), Decode({ path : Str, message : Str }), Wire(Str), Server(ServerError), Aborted({ at : U64, error : ServerError }), Transport(Str), WebSocket([Closed(Ws.Closure), Closing, Adapter(Str)]), Migration({ name : Str, problem : MigrationProblem })]
items.docs:
Why a reified function is not SurrealQL, or a schema is not one
SurrealDB can create. Every rejection names the construct. A live
session adds six: `Decode` for a value of the server that does not
fit the Roc type it is read as, with the path to it when the reader
names one (`result.row.temp_c`, else empty), `Wire` for bytes from
the server that are not what the protocol says, `Server` for a
request or a statement that the server refused, by its kind,
`Aborted` for a transaction that a statement failed, `Transport`
for a post over HTTP that the platform could not do, and
`WebSocket` for an error of the WebSocket adapter (roc-websocket's
`Ws.Error`): the connection ended (`Closed`, with how), it is
closing (`Closing`), or a tag of the adapter, as `Str.inspect`
writes it (`Adapter`, such as `Tcp(TimedOut)` or `Refused("..")`).
`at` of `Aborted` is the place of the prepared statement that
failed it (`Transaction.then`): 0 for the first, and the count of
them for the `COMMIT`, such as a `Conflict`. Every other statement
of the transaction is rolled back, or did not run. `Migration` is a
migration file or a history that the runner refuses (`name` is the
file, "" for `Surreal.check`): see `MigrationProblem`.
items.head: Error

items.name: MigrationProblem
items.signature: [Changed, OutOfOrder, Edit, Text(Str), Legacy, Level({ found : U64 }), Unplanned(List(Str))]
items.docs:
Why a migration does not run:

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Changed` | The database applied the file, and its text changed after that (the checksum) |
| `OutOfOrder` | The file is not applied, and a later file of the list is |
| `Edit` | The file still has a `-- reify: edit` line: write the value it asks for, then remove the line |
| `Text(why)` | The runner does not read the file: its header, a `BEGIN` or `COMMIT`, an index and a write on one table in one section, two files with one name |
| `Legacy` | The header has `target V3`: a file for SurrealDB 3, from 0.0.3 or before. With 0.0.3, raise the database to level 4 and squash the files into one `V4` file that `replaces` them; then upgrade |
| `Level(l)` | The database is at a compatibility level below 4 (`found`), such as a SurrealDB 3 datastore upgraded to SurrealDB 4. `name` is "". Raise it with `ALTER DATABASE COMPATIBILITY 4` |
| `Unplanned(statements)` | `Surreal.check`: the schema has changes that no migration file has |
items.head: MigrationProblem

items.name: ServerError
items.signature:
[
		Exists({ what : Str, name : Str, message : Str }),
		NotFound({ what : Str, name : Str, message : Str }),
		Unique({ table : Str, index : Str, fields : List(Str), value : Str, record : Str, message : Str }),
		Index({ index : Str, value : Str, record : Str, message : Str }),
		Assert({ table : Str, field : Str, record : Str, value : Str, condition : Str, message : Str }),
		Type({ table : Str, field : Str, record : Str, expected : Str, found : Str, message : Str }),
		Check({ table : Str, name : Str, message : Str }),
		Referenced({ record : Str, by : Str, message : Str }),
		Denied(Str),
		Parse(Str),
		Invalid(Str),
		Conflict(Str),
		Timeout(Str),
		Thrown({ text : Str, message : Str }),
		Other({ kind : Str, message : Str }),
	]
items.docs:
Why the server refused a request or a statement: the `kind` of its
error, and for the kind `Internal` (and a `Validation` of a type),
what its message says when the message has the form SurrealDB 4.0.1
writes. Each keeps the message.

| Tag | The server's error |
| --- | --- |
| `Exists` | `AlreadyExists`: `what` is the details' kind (`Record`, `Table`, ..), `name` the record id or the name |
| `NotFound` | `NotFound`, as `Exists`: a table, a record, a method |
| `Unique` | A unique index of the schema the session knows (`Session.knowing`) already holds the value: its table and fields (SurrealQL paths) |
| `Index` | The same for an index the session does not know |
| `Assert` | A field's `ASSERT` fails: the field, the record, the value and the condition |
| `Type` | A value does not fit the field's `TYPE` (`Validation` with details `InvalidRequest`) |
| `Check` | A `.check(name, ..)` of the schema that is an event fails (a check that a field holds is an `Assert`) |
| `Referenced` | A delete of a record that a link with `Reject` points at: `by` is the linking record (a root link) or `table.path` (a nested link) |
| `Denied` | `NotAllowed`, a post that HTTP refuses with 401 or 403, or a signup, a signin or a token that the server refuses (`Session.open!`) |
| `Parse` | `Validation` whose message is a parse error |
| `Invalid` | Any other `Validation`, such as a protected variable |
| `Conflict` | `Query` with `TransactionConflict`: the transaction can be retried |
| `Timeout` | `Query` with `TimedOut` |
| `Thrown` | `Thrown`: a `THROW`, with its text |
| `Other` | Any other kind, or a message of another form |
items.head: ServerError

items.name: message
items.docs: The server's message, as it sent it.

items.name: Value
items.signature:
[
		None,
		Bool(Bool),
		Int(I64),
		Float(F64),
		Decimal(Dec),
		Str(Str),
		Datetime(Str),
		Duration(U64),
		Record({ table : Str, key : Str }),
		Ref({ table : Str, key : Value }),
		Array(List(Value)),
		Object(List({ name : Str, value : Value })),
		I8(I8),
		U8(U8),
		I16(I16),
		U16(U16),
		I32(I32),
		U32(U32),
		U64(U64),
		F16(F32),
		F32(F32),
		Regex(Str),
		BigDecimal(Str),
		Date(I32),
		Time(U64),
		Timestamp({ secs : I64, nanos : U32 }),
		Interval({ months : I32, days : I32, micros : I64 }),
		Geometry(Value),
		Raw({ cbor : Cbor.Value, literal : Str }),
	]
items.docs:
One SurrealQL value, as a parameter, a seed or a default. `Float` and
`Decimal` stay apart because SurrealDB keeps them apart. `Record` is a
record id with a text key, and `Ref` one with a key of any value, such
as the array of a time series key.

The sized numbers of SurrealDB (`I8` to `U64`, `F16` and `F32`) are
apart from `Int` (`i64`) and `Float` (`f64`): their literal has the
suffix of the type (`5u8`), and CBOR v2 tags them (180 to 188). The
other types of CBOR v2: `Regex` (tag 193) and `BigDecimal` (192) hold
their text, `Date` (100) the days since 1970-01-01, `Time` (189) the
nanoseconds since midnight, `Timestamp` (190) the seconds and
nanoseconds since 1970 with no time zone, and `Interval` (191) the
months, the days and the microseconds. `Geometry` holds the GeoJSON
object of a geometry (`{ type: 'Point', coordinates: [1f, 2f] }`):
its literal is that object, which SurrealDB reads as a geometry, and
its CBOR is the geometry tag (88 to 94), since a plain object in a
var stays an object (verified on 4.0.1). `Raw` is a value of the
server that goes back to it as it came, such as the value of a live
diff patch, with its literal for the readable form of a request.
items.head: Value

items.name: literal
items.docs: The value as source text: `'it\'s'`, `20dec`, `customer:⟨ada⟩`, `{ a: 1 }`.

items.name: cbor
items.docs:
The value as CBOR, as a request of SurrealDB 4 takes it in its
`vars`: the second printer of a value, next to `literal`, and equal
to it on the server by value and by `type::of`. NONE is tag 6, a
decimal tag 10 and its text, a datetime tag 12 and `[secs, nanos]`,
a duration tag 14, a record id tag 8, a geometry tags 88 to 94, and
each type of CBOR v2 its tag (180 to 193, 100). A decimal of more
than 28 significant digits is refused: SurrealDB rounds such a var,
and refuses such a literal. An object with a name twice is refused,
as the server refuses a map with a key twice.

items.name: repeated_name
items.signature: List({ name : Str, value : Value }) -> Try(Str, [NotFound])
items.docs:
The first name in `fields` that a field before it also has.

`cbor` checks the names with this, and does not use
`Cbor.ValueMap.from_list`, which encodes and sorts the keys, and whose
error holds a `Cbor.Value`: in an optimised build, that code and the
`Str.inspect` of any `Cbor.Value` added about 5 s to the build of
every program that sends a request. An object has few fields. The
error text is the text that `Str.inspect` gave for the key.

items.name: vars
items.signature: List({ name : Str, value : Value }) -> Try(Cbor.Value, Error)
items.docs:
The `vars` map of a request: one entry per name, each value as
`cbor` prints it.

items.name: cbor_decimal
items.docs:
Tag 10 and the text of the decimal. Leading zeros are not
significant; the trailing zero of `Dec.to_str` (`20.0`) is counted,
which only makes the check stricter.

items.name: cbor_datetime
items.docs:
Tag 12 and `[secs, nanos]` of a datetime in the one form that
`Surreal.Datetime` holds: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, a fraction of one to
nine digits, and `Z`.

items.name: days_from_civil
items.docs: The day number of a date, counting from 1970-01-01.

items.name: cbor_geometry
items.docs:
The geometry tag of a GeoJSON object: 88 a point `[x, y]`, 89 a line
of points, 90 a polygon of lines, 91 to 93 the multi forms, 94 a
collection.

items.name: int_of
items.docs: The integer of an `Int` or of a sized integer value.

items.name: sized_float
items.docs:
A float of a sized type with its suffix (`1.5f32`). The non-finite
values have no literal, so they are a cast: `<f32>NaN`.

items.name: date_text
items.docs:
The date of a day number counted from 1970-01-01, as SurrealDB reads
it: `2026-11-13`, `-0001-01-01`, `+10000-01-01`.

items.name: clock_text
items.docs:
The time of day of the nanoseconds since midnight: `12:30:00`,
`12:30:00.5`. The fraction has no trailing zeros.

items.name: interval_text
items.signature: { months : I32, days : I32, micros : I64 } -> Str
items.docs:
An interval in ISO 8601: `P1M2DT3.5S`. Each part has its own sign,
as SurrealDB reads it (`P1M-2D`).

items.name: fraction
items.docs:
The digits of a fraction of `width` digits, without trailing zeros:
500000000 of 9 is `5`.

items.name: civil_from_days
items.docs: The year, month and day of a day number counted from 1970-01-01.

items.name: pad
items.docs: A number in at least `width` digits, with leading zeros.

items.name: float
items.docs:
A float with the `f` suffix, so a whole number stays a float. SurrealQL
spells the two non-finite values `NaN` and `Infinity`.

items.name: duration
items.docs:
A duration of `nanos` nanoseconds as a literal in the largest units
that fit: `1d`, `1w`, `1h30m`, `0ns`.

items.name: quote
items.docs: A string literal in single quotes.

items.name: ident
items.docs:
A table or field name, bare when SurrealQL reads it as a name and in
angle brackets otherwise (`⟨x y⟩`, `⟨select⟩`).

items.name: member
items.docs:
A name after a dot or an object key. Words such as `value` and `select`
are fine there (verified), so only a name that is not plain is bracketed.

items.name: record_id
items.docs:
A record id. The key is always bracketed, so any key is one token:
`customer:⟨o'neil⟩`, `customer:⟨x y⟩`.

items.name: record_ref
items.docs:
A record id with a key of any value: `t:⟨key⟩` for a text key, as
`record_id`, and `t:[..]` for an array key, the key of a time series.

items.name: keywords
items.docs:
Names SurrealQL does not accept bare as a table or a field. Found by
running each candidate word against SurrealDB 4.0.1.

items.name: is_plain
items.docs: A name made of lower case letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit.

items.name: escape
items.docs:
Text as it goes between quotes: `\`, the quote, and control characters
are escaped. Inside angle brackets, `⟩` is escaped too.

items.name: Uuid
items.docs:
The uuid of a live query: CBOR tag 37 and a byte string of 16 bytes.
SurrealDB gives one for each `LIVE SELECT`, and puts it in each
notice of that query.
items.head: Uuid

items.name: from_bytes
items.docs: The uuid of these 16 bytes.

items.name: to_str
items.docs: The text form: `8-4-4-4-12` hex digits.

items.name: parser_for
items.signature: Cbor -> (Cbor.Reader -> Try({ value : Uuid, rest : Cbor.Reader }, [InvalidCbor(U64), MissingRequiredField(Str)]))

items.name: signin
items.signature: U64, { user : Str, pass : Str } -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List({ user : Str, pass : Str }) }
items.docs: `signin` as a system user of the server.

items.name: access
items.signature: U64, Str, { ns : Str, db : Str, access : Str }, List((Cbor.Value, Cbor.Value)) -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Cbor.Value) }
items.docs:
`signup` or `signin` (`method`) of a record user: one map of the
namespace, the database, the access method (`ac`) and the variables
of its `SIGNUP` or `SIGNIN` query. The reply is the token.

items.name: authenticate
items.signature: U64, Str -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Str) }
items.docs: `authenticate`: the session is the user of a token.

items.name: invalidate
items.signature: U64 -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Str) }
items.docs: `invalidate`: the session is no one.

items.name: use_db
items.signature: U64, Str, Str -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Str) }
items.docs: `use`: the namespace and the database of the session.

items.name: query
items.signature: U64, Str, Cbor.Value -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Cbor.Value) }
items.docs:
`query`: one text of statements, such as `Watch.request`, and the
map of its vars: the value of each `$name` of the text. Every
statement of the text sees them, and no later request does. A map
with no entry is left out.

items.name: kill
items.signature: U64, Uuid -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Uuid) }
items.docs: `kill`: the end of a live query. SurrealDB sends `KILLED` for it.

items.name: Policy
items.docs: What a delete does to the rows that link to the deleted row.
items.head: Policy

items.name: Rule
items.signature:
[
		Assert({ path : Str, cond : Str }),
		Check({ name : Str, cond : Str, holders : List({ path : Str, cond : Str }) }),
		Index({ paths : List(Str), unique : Bool }),
		SearchIndex({ path : Str, kind : Str, spec : Str, analyzers : List(Str) }),
		Default({ path : Str, value : Str }),
		Computed({ path : Str, expr : Str }),
		Readonly(Str),
		Comment({ path : Str, text : Str }),
		OnDelete({ table : Str, policy : Schema.Policy }),
		OnDeleteAt({ path : Str, policy : Schema.Policy }),
		Changefeed(U64),
		Permit({ actions : List(Schema.Action), grant : Schema.Grant }),
		PermitField({ path : Str, actions : List(Schema.Action), grant : Schema.Grant }),
	]
items.docs:
One clause of the builder, translated. Paths are spelled as a field
definition names them (`items[*].qty`). Conditions are over `$value`,
a row check is over `$after`, a computed value is over `$this`.
items.head: Rule

items.name: Action
items.docs:
What a permission is for: a statement of a record user that reads
or writes the table or the field.
items.head: Action

items.name: Grant
items.docs:
A permission: the rows that the condition keeps (`WHERE`, over the
row, which may read the session: `$auth.id`), every row, or none.
items.head: Grant

items.name: Defined
items.signature:
[
		Table({ source : Types.Source, rules : List(Schema.Rule), problems : List(Ql.Error) }),
		Function(Try(List(Schema.Function), Ql.Error)),
		Read({ name : Str, row_ty : Code.Ty }),
		Access(Try(Str, Ql.Error)),
		Analyzer({ name : Str, line : Str }),
	]
items.docs:
A finished table definition, the database functions of one
`Surreal.function`, or a read row of a table, which writes no
statement and is checked against the stored row: what
`Surreal.schema` takes.
items.head: Defined

items.name: Function
items.signature: { name : Str, params : List(Code.Ty), result : Code.Ty, body : Str }
items.docs:
A database function, translated: `$a1`, `$a2`, .. have the types of
`params`, and `body` is the value it returns.
items.head: Function

items.name: analyzer
items.docs:
`DEFINE ANALYZER`, which a full-text index names: a statement of
the database, before every table.

items.name: search_index
items.signature: Str, Str, Str, List(Str) -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A full-text or a vector index on the field at `path`: `kind` names
it, `spec` is what follows `FIELDS path` (`FULLTEXT ANALYZER a BM25
HIGHLIGHTS`, `HNSW DIMENSION 3 DIST COSINE TYPE F64`), and
`analyzers` the analyzer it names, which the schema must define.

items.name: access
items.signature: { name : Str, table : Str, content : Try(Str, Ql.Error), cond : Try(Str, Ql.Error), token : Try(U64, [Unset]), session : Try(U64, [Unset]) } -> Schema.Defined
items.docs:
`DEFINE ACCESS name ON DATABASE TYPE RECORD`: a signup is a
`CREATE` of the content, a signin a `SELECT` of the row that the
condition keeps, each over the variables of the RPC as `$name`.
The durations are nanoseconds; one that is not given is
SurrealDB's default (a token of 1 hour, a session with no end).

items.name: tables
items.docs:
The tables of the definitions, where a link finds its table: each
stored row, and each read row with the name of its table.

items.name: Hop
items.docs:
One step to a link: a field, each element of a list, the arm of a
union (the value there is that arm), or one item of an array.
items.head: Hop

items.name: Site
items.signature: { hops : List(Schema.Hop), target : Code.Ty, optional : Bool }
items.docs:
A `Link` or `Id` in a row. A list of links ends in `Each`. `optional`
is True when the link's own field is `?:`.
items.head: Site

items.name: check
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, Str, Code.Graph -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A row check, placed by one rule: when it reads only one top-level
field, it is that field's `ASSERT`; when it reads more, it is the
`ASSERT` of one of them (`place_checks`), or else an event over
`$after`; when it reads none, it is an error. `extensions` give
the forms of the calls of each clause here (`Translate.form`).

items.name: holders
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Code.Graph, List(Types.Field) -> List({ path : Str, cond : Str })
items.docs:
The fields that can hold a check over several fields as their `ASSERT`:
each required field that the check reads, with the check over `$value`
for that field and `$this` for the others. `$this` is the row with the
new values of every field (verified), so the other fields are final.
It is empty when the check reads a field with no definition (the key).

items.name: place_checks
items.docs:
A check over several fields is the `ASSERT` of its first holder that
is not read-only and has no field permission: SurrealDB runs the
assert of a required field on every write, but not the assert of a
read-only field that does not change (verified), and an event has no
field permission. With no such holder, it stays an event.

items.name: permit
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, List(Schema.Action), [Where(Code.Graph), Full, No] -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A permission of the table for `actions`: the condition over the
row, a `filter`'s (`Translate.table_row`), or `FULL` or `NONE`.

items.name: permit_field
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, Code.Graph, List(Schema.Action), [Where(Code.Graph), Full, No] -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs: A permission of the field at a path for `actions`, as `permit`.

items.name: grant
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, [Where(Code.Graph), Full, No] -> Try(Schema.Grant, Ql.Error)

items.name: permissions
items.signature: Str, List({ actions : List(Schema.Action), grant : Schema.Grant }), Bool -> Try(Str, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
`PERMISSIONS FOR select WHERE .., FOR create, update FULL`: one
`FOR` for each permission, in the order given. Each action is in
one at most. A table names the actions that no permission names
`NONE`, which is SurrealDB's default for a table; a field leaves
them out, and SurrealDB's default for a field is `FULL`.

items.name: placed
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Code.Graph, List(Types.Field) -> [NoField, OnField({ name : Str, cond : Str }), Several]
items.docs:
Where a predicate over a record goes. It is evaluated with the record
holding one field at a time, bound to `$value`: it evaluates exactly
when it reads nothing outside that field.

items.name: assert
items.docs: A predicate on one field: its `ASSERT`.

items.name: assert_each
index
items.docs: An index on one path or on a record of paths.

items.name: index_path
items.docs: An index path. An edge's `from` and `to` are SurrealDB's `in` and `out`.

items.name: default_by
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, Code.Graph, Code.Graph -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs: A default that is an expression over `$this`, which may call `Rand`.

items.name: computed
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, Code.Graph, Code.Graph -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs: A value SurrealDB computes on every write, over `$this`. It may call `Rand`.

items.name: created_now
items.docs:
The time of the first write, kept: `VALUE time::now() READONLY`
(verified: an update keeps it, a create cannot set it).

items.name: changefeed
items.docs: A change history of this many nanoseconds, on the table line.

items.name: skipped
items.docs: Fields with no definition: the record key, and an edge's two ends.

items.name: sites
items.docs:
Every `Link` and `Id` in a row, as `Types.link_sites` lists them, with
the steps that reach each one. The ends of an edge are not listed:
SurrealDB's `ENFORCED` relation checks them and deletes the edge with
either end.

items.name: site_path
items.docs: The field a site is in: a list of links is the list.

items.name: shape
items.docs: The shape `Types.link_sites` gives the same site.

items.name: is_native
items.docs:
A site SurrealDB's own `REFERENCE` covers: a root field, or a root
list of links. `REFERENCE` is refused on a nested field (SF).

items.name: mentions
items.docs:
A condition over a row of the linking table: the link at `hops` is the
deleted row, `$before.id`.

items.name: unset
items.docs:
The `SET` that unsets a nested link: an optional field becomes `NONE`,
a link leaves its list, and an element of a list of objects that holds
the link leaves the list, as native `UNSET` does to a list of links.

items.name: script
items.docs:
The schema script: every `DEFINE FUNCTION`, then every `DEFINE ANALYZER`, then every `DEFINE TABLE`,
then every view, then every field, then the indexes, the row-check
events, the delete events and the access methods, so that no statement names a function or
a table defined later. A view that calls a function needs it defined
first (verified).

items.name: script_lines
items.docs: The statements of `script`, one for each item, in its order.

items.name: FieldInfo
items.signature: { table : Str, path : Str, ty : Str, default : Try(Str, [NoDefault]) }
items.docs:
A field of a table as `script` defines it: `table` and `path` as
the `DEFINE FIELD` names them, its type and its `DEFAULT`.
items.head: FieldInfo

items.name: field_infos
items.docs:
The fields of the tables of a schema, with the values that
`field` prints, before they are printed.

items.name: Step
items.signature:
[
		Define(Str),
		Remove(Str),
		DropField({ table : Str, path : Str }),
		DropTable(Str),
		Fill({ line : Str, table : Str, path : Str, value : Try(Str, [NoDefault]) }),
		Retype({ line : Str, table : Str, path : Str, from : Str, to : Str, value : Try(Str, [NoDefault]) }),
	]
items.docs:
One step of a migration. `Remove` loses no row: an index, an
event, a function, an analyzer, an access or a view. `DropField` and
`DropTable` remove the data of the field or the table. `Fill` is a
new field on a table that has rows: `line` defines it, and the rows
get `value`, its `DEFAULT`. `Retype` is a field whose type changed
and does not take every old value: the rows convert to `to`, and
`value` is its `DEFAULT`.
items.head: Step

items.name: migration_steps
items.docs:
The steps from the statements of the schema `old` to those of `new`:
what `old` has and `new` does not, from the last to the first, then
each statement of `new` that is new or changed, in its order. What
is on a table that `new` does not have goes with the table. Only a
statement whose text changed is in the steps.

items.name: fill_value
items.docs:
The value that the rows of a table get for a new field: its
`DEFAULT` from `fields`, or `NoDefault`. A `DEFAULT` is not given
to the rows that are there (verified). A field in an object or a
list, an optional field and the key get no value.

items.name: field_type
items.docs:
The `TYPE` of a `DEFINE FIELD`: the words after `TYPE`, up to the
next clause. "" when it has none.

items.name: unwrapped
items.docs: The type without `option<..>`, and whether it had it.

items.name: members
items.docs: The members of a union type, split at the top level only.

items.name: widens
items.docs:
Whether a field of type `new` takes every value of type `old`: the
same members and more, `option` kept or added, `any`, `number` for
each number type, or a sized number type that holds each value of
a smaller one (`u8` in `i16`, `u32` in `int`, `f32` in `float`).

items.name: number_types
items.docs: The number types of SurrealDB 4.

items.name: wider_numbers
items.docs:
The number types that hold each value of a sized one, with no loss
(verified on SurrealDB 4.0.1: a field of such a type takes the value).

items.name: Entry
items.signature: { kind : Str, name : Str, on : Str, line : Str }
items.docs:
A statement of `script` by what it defines: `kind` is the word after
`DEFINE`, `on` the table of a field, an index or an event
(`DATABASE` for an access), or "" for the others.
items.head: Entry

items.name: is_view
items.docs: A view is `DEFINE TABLE OVERWRITE name TYPE NORMAL AS SELECT ..`.

items.name: words
items.docs: The words of a line, a name in `⟨ ⟩` with a space in it one word.

items.name: functions
items.docs:
One `DEFINE FUNCTION` for each name. A function that two
`Surreal.function` entries reach is written once; two different bodies
with one name are a `BadSchema`.

items.name: function_line
items.docs: `DEFINE FUNCTION OVERWRITE fn::name($a1: T1, ..) -> R { RETURN body };`

items.name: analyzed
items.signature: { source : Types.Source, rules : List(Schema.Rule), problems : List(Ql.Error) }, List(Str) -> Try({}, Ql.Error)
items.docs: Each full-text index of a table names an analyzer of the schema.

items.name: Parts
items.signature: { tables : List(Str), views : List(Str), fields : List(Str), indexes : List(Str), checks : List(Str), deletes : List(Str), names : List(Str) }
items.head: Parts

items.name: statements
items.signature: { source : Types.Source, rules : List(Schema.Rule), problems : List(Ql.Error) }, Types.Registry -> Try(Schema.Parts, Ql.Error)

items.name: key_def
items.docs:
The field definitions with one for a text key that a clause gives
a default: `.default_by(|r| r.id, |_| Surreal.Rand.ulid())` is
`DEFINE FIELD id .. TYPE string DEFAULT rand::ulid()`, and a create
with no key gets that key (`Table.create_new`). A key with no
default has no definition, and SurrealDB makes a random key.

items.name: view
items.docs:
A view: `DEFINE TABLE .. AS SELECT ..`. SurrealDB fills it from its
query, so it has no field definitions, and it takes no rule: a view is
read-only.

items.name: Link
items.signature: { site : Schema.Site, table : Str, policy : Schema.Policy }
items.head: Link

items.name: policy_of
items.signature: Str, Schema.Site, List(Schema.Rule), Types.Registry -> Try(Schema.Link, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The policy of one site: `on_delete_at` for its path, else `on_delete`
for its target table, else `Reject`.

items.name: known
items.signature: Str, List(Str), List(Str), Schema.Rule -> Try({}, Ql.Error)
items.docs: A clause's path must be a field the table defines.

items.name: used
items.docs: A delete clause must name a link of the table.

items.name: field_default
items.docs:
The `DEFAULT` of a field: the `??` default of the type, or a
`default` or `default_by` clause. Two are a `BadSchema`.

items.name: field
items.signature: Str, Types.FieldDef, List(Schema.Rule), List(Schema.Link) -> Try(Str, Ql.Error)
items.docs: One `DEFINE FIELD`, with what the clauses add to it.

items.name: delete_event
items.signature: Str, Schema.Link -> Try({ name : Str, line : Str }, Ql.Error)
items.docs: The event on the target table that does a nested link's policy.

items.name: slug
items.docs: A name part made of letters, digits and `_`: `items[*].qty` is `items_qty`.

items.name: index_name
items.docs: The name of the index of `Def.unique` or `Def.index` on these paths.

items.name: check_name
items.docs: The name of the event of `Def.check`.

items.name: Known
items.signature: { index : Str, table : Str, fields : List(Str) }
items.docs: A unique index that the schema defines: its name, table and paths.
items.head: Known

items.name: unique_indexes
items.docs:
The unique indexes of the definitions, which `Session.knowing`
keeps so that a violation of one names its fields.

items.name: violation
items.docs:
An error of the kind `Internal`, read from its message where it has
a form that SurrealDB 4.0.1 writes for a constraint (verified). The
message of a type error is the same, but its kind is `Validation`
(`Surreal.server_error` sends it here):

| Message | Tag |
| --- | --- |
| ``Database index `i` already contains v, with record `r` `` | `Unique` for a known index, else `Index` |
| ``Found v for field `f`, with record `r`, but field must conform to: c`` | `Assert` |
| ``Couldn't coerce value for field `f` of `r`: Expected `t` but found `v` `` | `Type` |
| ``Cannot delete `r` as it is referenced by `b` with an ON DELETE REJECT clause`` | `Referenced` (a root link) |
| ``Error while processing event e: An error occurred: t`` | `Check` when `e` and `t` are those of a `Def.check`; `Referenced` when `e` is the delete event of a nested link; else `Thrown` |
| ``Error while processing event e: m`` | What `m` is |

Any other message is `Other`. A record id is as the server writes
it, `vet:a` or `` `my t`:k ``; the table is the part before `:`.

items.name: thrown_in
items.docs:
The text that an event threw: a `Def.check` throws `table: name`
from the event `table_check_<name>`, and the delete event of a
nested link `record is referenced by table.path`.

items.name: table_of
items.docs:
The table of a record id as the server writes it: `vet` of `vet:a`,
`my t` of `` `my t`:k ``.

items.name: no_cycle
items.signature: List({ source : Types.Source, rules : List(Schema.Rule), problems : List(Ql.Error) }), Types.Registry -> Try({}, Ql.Error)

items.name: Id
items.docs:
A typed record id: `customer:⟨ada⟩`. The type parameter `row` ties the
id to its row type: no value holds it, and the type checker keeps an
`Id(Customer)` from an `Id(Product)`. The reifier gives it as the
type argument of the `Named` (`Types.row_of`), so a captured id holds
only its table and key.
items.head: Id(row)

items.name: Created
items.docs:
A row that `Table.create_new` or `Table.insert_new` made, with the
key that the server gave it: its `Id`, and its other fields as
stored. `new` is the row without its `id`, so a `Created(Customer,
{ name : Str })` reads `made.id.key()` and `made.fields.name`, and
`customers.link(made.id.key())` links to it.

items.name: Link
items.docs:
A stored link. `fetched` holds the row when the application has it (seed
data, a row read back). In a clause, `get` is a traversal: `customer.name`.
items.head: Link(row)

items.name: get
items.docs:
The row. A link that was not fetched has none, and this crashes: the
row lives in the database, so only a clause can read through it.

items.name: id
items.docs:
The record id the link holds: the id itself in a clause. In a clause
the field `link.id` is the same. The field `fetched` has no meaning
in the database, so a clause that reads it is refused.

items.docs: Equal when the ids are equal.

items.name: Linked
items.docs:
A read view of a link: the linked row, read as a field of this row,
so `p.owner.name` is the traversal `owner.name` with no `.get()`. It
is for reads only. A row that holds one has no encoder, so a write of
it is a type error, and the stored row of its table holds a `Link`
at the same place (`Table.define_read` checks it). The linked row is
an alias of a record or a nominal over one, also a row that links to
its own table (`Linked(Owner)` with `referred_by ?: Link(Owner)`), or a
read row. It finds its table by its row, the type argument, as a `Link`.
items.head: Linked(row)

items.name: linked

items.name: Datetime

A SurrealDB `datetime`, held as UTC ISO 8601 with a `Z`

times are equal strings. Make one with `datetime`.
items.head: Datetime

items.docs:

the `Z` kept, `...59Z` would sort after `...59.5Z`.

items.docs:
A datetime from `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, an optional fraction of up to
nine digits, and `Z`. Other offsets are refused: the order of the text

`TimeKey` is a time series, and `Query.between` reads one range of it.
items.head: TimeKey(s)

items.name: time

equal, and `from <= time < to`. For a reference result in Roc.
